name: Sprocket
text:
Do it: Auto-apply all safe changes immediately, then log the rest for review.

This keeps the loop fast and frictionless—no waiting for human approval on trivial fixes. The trade-off is accepting a small risk of applying a change that later proves harmful, but the review log ensures we can catch and roll back errors quickly. Safe changes are defined as those with no side effects beyond the prompt batch, like formatting tweaks or obvious typos.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk is that "safe" is subjective until proven by failure—what’s trivial to one system may cascade in another. A better alternative: auto-apply only changes with a pre-approved, narrow scope (e.g., typo fixes, formatting) and route the rest for review. Settle it by testing the auto-apply on a non-critical branch first, measuring harm before expanding.
